mxCell.value: eClaims — Solution Architecture · Six-Layer Microservices on AWS
Project: YCompany eClaims | Version 1.0 | Author: Utsav Verma (Senior Staff Engineer, Nagarro) | Date: 07-Jul-2026 | Classification: Confidential

Layer 1 — Client / Edge
Web · Staff · Partner Portals

Layer 2 — API Gateway / Ingress
WAF · CDN · ALB · Auth

Layer 4 — Async / Messaging
EventBridge · SQS · SNS · Lambda

Notes & Conventions:
1. All external traffic is HTTPS / TLS 1.2+. Inter-service calls carry an OAuth2 JWT (15-min access / 7-day refresh), validated against the Auth Service.
2. Layer 6 platform services (IAM/SSO, KMS, CloudWatch, X-Ray, CloudTrail, CI/CD, Terraform) are cross-cutting and govern every layer above — shown by a representative dashed flow (KMS → data at rest).
3. All data is encrypted at rest (KMS AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+); every claim document and customer communication is archived in S3 for audit and compliance.
4. Solid arrows = request / data flow (protocol labelled). Dashed arrows = cross-cutting / governance / association.

Why no managed API Gateway? Classic API-Gateway capabilities are already delivered by existing components (verified against the SAD):
Routing / dispatch → ALB (Multi-AZ, /claims /auth)   |   AuthN / AuthZ → Auth Service (OAuth2/JWT) + RBAC + Okta SSO, ALB OIDC offload
Rate limiting / throttling → AWS WAF + Shield (edge rate-based rules)   |   Caching → CloudFront (edge) + ElastiCache Redis (data, <100 ms)
Canary / blue-green → CodePipeline + CodeDeploy, ALB weighted target groups   |   Circuit breaker / retries → service-level breakers + exponential backoff
Distributed tracing → CloudWatch + X-Ray   |   Request validation → in-service (FastAPI + Pydantic)
A managed API Gateway would only add per-API-key usage plans / metering — not required, since partners integrate via the Partner Portal, not raw metered APIs.
Each domain owns its data and services; domains integrate only through published events on the messaging backbone (loose coupling).
Event & Messaging Backbone — AWS EventBridge · SQS · SNS
Shared Platform — IAM / SSO · KMS encryption · Central Document Store (S3) · Data Warehouse (Redshift) · Observability & Immutable Audit (CloudWatch / X-Ray / CloudTrail)
